text:
Kaapo Kakko got to play in front of a Finnish crowd last week when Seattle met Carolina twice in the Global Series in Finland. NHL.com called the game special to him "despite loss," and the Kraken lost both. It was a fitting snapshot of his season: a nice story wrapped around a team that's struggling.

His own line is solid. He has 13 points in 18 games, ten of them assists, in about 14 minutes a night. But the shot volume is strikingly low, 15 shots on goal all season and 1.9 expected goals, and he's turned that into three goals. The Kraken have also scored 7.3 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and at 5v5 they get only 43% of the expected goals (chance quality) when he's out there.

Some of that is context. Evolving-Hockey had him playing with teammates in the bottom 8% by impact last season, yet still 73rd of 401 forwards by wins above replacement. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows a signature: 19% of his setups come from behind the net, more than double a typical forward. He's a playmaker who needs more shooters around him.
headline: Kakko, the passer, after a trip home
